name: Daniela Torres
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss Nicaragua 2015 on 7 March 2015 at age 25, representing Nicaragua at Miss Universe 2015 and achieving a Top 5 finish in the National Costume category.
starting_point: Born in Managua, Nicaragua; was a student of tourism business administration before entering pageantry. Trained with Puerto Rican pageant coach Grace Fontecha.
current_position: Model and beauty queen from Nicaragua; current professional status beyond pageantry not widely documented in reviewed sources.

trajectory.title: Competed at Miss Continentes Unidos
trajectory.description: Competed at Miss Continentes Unidos 2013, gaining early pageant experience on the international stage.

trajectory.title: Won Miss Nicaragua 2015
trajectory.description: Crowned Miss Nicaragua 2015 on March 7 at the Ruben Dario Theater, winning five special awards: Miss Photogenic, Best Smile, Miss Cielo, Best Hair, and Miss MedSpa.

trajectory.title: Competed at Miss Universe 2015
trajectory.description: Represented Nicaragua at Miss Universe 2015 in Las Vegas, achieving a Top 5 finish in the National Costume category among 81 contestants.

trajectory.title: Post-pageant media appearances
trajectory.description: Gained media attention across Central America for her strong performance at Miss Universe, being described as the strongest Central American candidate.

trajectory.title: Completed reign as Miss Nicaragua
trajectory.description: Completed her year-long reign as Miss Nicaragua, having represented her country at the international level and participated in various national events and charitable activities throughout her tenure.

name: Lindsey Jordan (Snail Mail)
milestone_by_age_26: Signed a recording contract with Matador Records in September 2017 at age 18, and released debut studio album 'Lush' in June 2018 to critical acclaim, reaching #2 on the Billboard Heatseekers Albums chart and earning widespread indie press coverage including Pitchfork's Best New Music designation.
starting_point: Born June 16, 1999 in Ellicott City, Maryland to a middle-class family; mother owns a lingerie store, father works for a textbook publisher. Started classical guitar lessons at age 5.
current_position: Active recording and touring musician as Snail Mail; released third album 'Ricochet' in 2026; resides in the United States.

trajectory.title: First live performance as Snail Mail
trajectory.description: Performed live for the first time as Snail Mail at age 15-16 in the Baltimore/D.C. DIY music scene.

trajectory.title: Released debut EP 'Habit'
trajectory.description: Released the EP 'Habit' on Sister Polygon Records, produced by members of Priests, attracting attention in the indie rock scene.

trajectory.title: Signed with Matador Records
trajectory.description: Signed a recording contract with Matador Records in September 2017 after tours with Waxahatchee, Girlpool, and Beach Fossils and an NPR Tiny Desk concert.

trajectory.title: Released debut album 'Lush'
trajectory.description: Released debut studio album 'Lush' in June 2018 to critical acclaim, reaching #2 on the Billboard Heatseekers Albums chart and earning Pitchfork's Best New Music designation.

trajectory.title: Released second album 'Valentine'
trajectory.description: Released sophomore album 'Valentine' produced by Brad Cook, expanding her sound with samples, synthesizers, and strings; performed on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

trajectory.title: Released third album 'Ricochet'
trajectory.description: Released third studio album 'Ricochet' featuring lusher string arrangements and denser electronic textures recorded with Aron Kobayashi Ritch of Momma.

name: Nikkie de Jager (NikkieTutorials)
milestone_by_age_26: Her YouTube video 'The Power of Makeup' went viral in 2015 at age 21, inspiring a global movement; Forbes named her one of the top 10 beauty influencers in 2017; she won the Shorty Award for YouTube Guru and Teen Choice Award for Choice Fashion/Beauty Web Star in 2017; and she became Global Beauty Adviser for Marc Jacobs Beauty in January 2019.
starting_point: Born March 2, 1994 in Wageningen, Netherlands; began watching makeup tutorials on YouTube inspired by MTV's The Hills at age 14. Transitioned at a young age with family support.
current_position: Dutch beauty YouTuber and makeup artist with ~15 million subscribers and 2.4 billion views; married Dylan Drossaers in 2022; continues creating content and collaborating with major beauty brands.

trajectory.title: Started YouTube channel NikkieTutorials
trajectory.description: Uploaded her first makeup tutorial video to YouTube at age 14, inspired by Lauren Conrad's makeup on MTV's The Hills.

trajectory.title: Signed with Colourfool Agency
trajectory.description: Enrolled in makeup coursework at B Academy in Amsterdam and signed with Colourfool Agency, beginning her professional makeup artist career.

trajectory.title: Head makeup artist for RTL 5 show
trajectory.description: Became the head makeup artist for the RTL 5 show 'I Can Make You a Supermodel' with Paul Fisher.

trajectory.title: 'The Power of Makeup' went viral
trajectory.description: Her YouTube video 'The Power of Makeup' went viral, inspiring a global movement of people showing their faces with and without makeup.

trajectory.title: Forbes top 10 beauty influencer and award wins
trajectory.description: Named one of Forbes' top 10 beauty influencers; won the Shorty Award for YouTube Guru and Teen Choice Award for Choice Fashion/Beauty Web Star.

trajectory.title: Global Beauty Adviser for Marc Jacobs Beauty
trajectory.description: Appointed as Global Beauty Adviser for Marc Jacobs Beauty in January 2019, integrated into the brand's product development process.

trajectory.title: Came out as transgender
trajectory.description: Publicly came out as transgender in a YouTube video titled 'I'm Coming Out' after being blackmailed, inspiring millions of fans worldwide.

trajectory.title: Married Dylan Drossaers
trajectory.description: Married Dylan Drossaers in 2022; continues as one of the biggest beauty stars on YouTube with nearly 15 million subscribers.

name: Naseem Shah
milestone_by_age_26: Made Test debut for Pakistan at age 16 in November 2019, becoming the ninth-youngest Test debutant; took a five-wicket haul at age 16 in December 2019 and became the youngest bowler to take a Test hat-trick in February 2020 at age 16.
starting_point: Born February 15, 2003 in Mayar, Lower Dir, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan into a Pashtun family; father was a farmer who opposed his cricket career. Mother died the day before his Test debut. Uncle facilitated his entry into Abdul Qadir Cricket Academy in Lahore.
current_position: Pakistani international fast bowler playing across all formats; currently active in international cricket and franchise leagues including PSL.

trajectory.title: First-class debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-class debut for Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited during the 2018-19 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy after being selected for Pakistan U-16 at age 13.

trajectory.title: Test debut for Pakistan
trajectory.description: Made his Test debut for Pakistan against Australia in November 2019 at the Gabba, becoming the ninth-youngest Test debutant in history.

trajectory.title: Five-wicket haul against Sri Lanka
trajectory.description: Took a five-wicket haul against Sri Lanka in December 2019, becoming the second-youngest bowler and youngest pace bowler to achieve the feat in Test cricket.

trajectory.title: Youngest Test hat-trick
trajectory.description: Became the youngest bowler to take a hat-trick in Test cricket at age 16 years and 359 days, against Bangladesh in February 2020.

trajectory.title: ODI and T20I debuts
trajectory.description: Made his ODI debut against the Netherlands in August 2022 and T20I debut against India in August 2022 at the Asia Cup.

trajectory.title: PSL and franchise cricket success
trajectory.description: Continued playing for Quetta Gladiators in the PSL and became a regular across all formats for Pakistan's national team.

trajectory.title: Active international career
trajectory.description: Continued as a key fast bowler for Pakistan across formats, playing Test series against South Africa and ODIs through 2025-2026.

name: Mujeeb Ur Rahman
milestone_by_age_26: Made ODI debut for Afghanistan at age 16 in December 2017, taking 4/24 on debut; became the youngest player to take a five-wicket haul in ODI cricket at age 16 in February 2018, and played in Afghanistan's first-ever Test match in June 2018.
starting_point: Born March 28, 2001 in Khost, Afghanistan; grew up in a mansion with private practicing facilities. Uncle Noor Ali Zadran is an Afghan international cricketer who ran a cricket academy where Mujeeb honed his skills.
current_position: Afghan international cricketer playing across all formats; active in franchise T20 leagues worldwide including BBL, IPL, and PSL; currently playing for Paarl Royals.

trajectory.title: ODI debut for Afghanistan
trajectory.description: Made his ODI debut for Afghanistan against Ireland on December 5, 2017, taking 4/24 on debut and winning Man of the Match.

trajectory.title: Youngest ODI five-wicket haul
trajectory.description: Became the youngest player to take a five-wicket haul in ODI cricket at age 16 years and 325 days, in February 2018.

trajectory.title: Afghanistan's first Test match
trajectory.description: Played in Afghanistan's inaugural Test match against India in June 2018, taking one wicket.

trajectory.title: IPL contract with Kings XI Punjab
trajectory.description: Secured an IPL contract worth INR 4 crore with Kings XI Punjab (now Punjab Kings) at age 17.

trajectory.title: ICC Cricket World Cup
trajectory.description: Represented Afghanistan at the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup, picking up 7 wickets in the tournament.

trajectory.title: T20 World Cup and franchise cricket
trajectory.description: Played a key role in Afghanistan's T20 World Cup campaign and was picked by Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL.

trajectory.title: ODI World Cup performance
trajectory.description: Represented Afghanistan at the 2023 ODI World Cup, taking 3/51 against England in a historic win.

trajectory.title: Continued international and franchise career
trajectory.description: Continued playing T20Is for Afghanistan and franchise cricket for Paarl Royals, remaining a key spin bowling asset.

name: Rema
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with Jonzing World/Mavin Records in 2019 at age 19; debut EP topped Apple Music Nigeria charts, and breakout single 'Dumebi' became a viral hit with 85M+ YouTube views, landing on Barack Obama's summer playlist.
starting_point: Born May 1, 2000 in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria into a Christian family; lost his father and elder brother at a young age and was raised by his mother. Discovered music in church and began rapping in secondary school.
current_position: Nigerian Afrobeats superstar; Grammy-nominated artist with global hits including 'Calm Down' remix with Selena Gomez reaching #3 on Billboard Hot 100; announced as performer at 2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony.

trajectory.title: Won Pikolo's Dream Alive talent show
trajectory.description: Won Season 2 of Pikolo's Dream Alive talent show in Benin City at age 13, signing briefly with Peak Entertainment.

trajectory.title: Signed with Jonzing World/Mavin Records
trajectory.description: Signed with D'Prince's Jonzing World label in partnership with Mavin Records after a viral freestyle on Instagram caught attention.

trajectory.title: Breakout single 'Dumebi'
trajectory.description: Released debut EP which topped Apple Music Nigeria charts; breakout single 'Dumebi' became a viral hit with 85M+ YouTube views and landed on Barack Obama's summer playlist.

trajectory.title: 'Calm Down' global breakthrough
trajectory.description: Released single 'Calm Down' which became a global phenomenon; the remix with Selena Gomez peaked at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and led the U.S. Afrobeats chart for a record 58 weeks.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Rave & Roses'
trajectory.description: Released debut studio album 'Rave & Roses' which reached #81 on the Billboard 200, cementing his status as a leading Afrobeats artist.

trajectory.title: Second album 'Heis' and Grammy nomination
trajectory.description: Released second album 'Heis' preceded by single 'Benin Boys' with Shallipopi; earned his first Grammy Award nomination for Best Global Music Album.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup opening ceremony performer
trajectory.description: Announced as a performer at the 2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony at SoFi Stadium, marking a career milestone in global recognition.

name: Shubman Gill
milestone_by_age_26: Named Player of the Tournament at the 2018 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup at age 18, scoring 418 runs at an average of 104.50; made ODI debut for India in January 2019 at age 19, and was bought by Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL for Rs 1.8 crore.
starting_point: Born September 8, 1999 in Fazilka, Punjab, India into a Punjabi Sikh family; father Lakhwinder Singh is a farmer who aspired to be a cricketer and moved the family to Mohali near the PCA Stadium for better training. Father bowled 500-700 balls to him daily from age 3.
current_position: Captain of India's Test and ODI teams; captain of Gujarat Titans in the IPL; scored 754 runs in a Test series against England in 2025, the fastest male batter to 2,000 ODI runs.

trajectory.title: Inter-District U16 record
trajectory.description: Scored 351 in Punjab's Inter-District U16 tournament, racking up an opening stand of 587 runs, establishing himself as a prodigy.

trajectory.title: List A and first-class debuts for Punjab
trajectory.description: Made his List A debut for Punjab in the Vijay Hazare Trophy, scoring a maiden century in his second match; made his first-class debut in the Ranji Trophy in November 2017.

trajectory.title: Player of the Tournament at U-19 World Cup
trajectory.description: Named Player of the Tournament at the 2018 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup, scoring 418 runs at an average of 104.50 as India won the title.

trajectory.title: ODI debut and IPL contract
trajectory.description: Made his ODI debut for India against New Zealand in January 2019; bought by Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL for Rs 1.8 crore.

trajectory.title: Historic Gabba Test victory
trajectory.description: Played a instrumental role in India's historic chase and Test victory against Australia at the Gabba, Brisbane in January 2021.

trajectory.title: Double century in ODIs
trajectory.description: Scored 208 against New Zealand in Hyderabad, his highest ODI score, becoming one of the youngest to hit an ODI double century.

trajectory.title: Appointed Test and ODI captain
trajectory.description: Appointed captain of India's Test and ODI teams at age 25; scored 754 runs in a five-match Test series against England, becoming the youngest Indian captain to win a Test overseas.

trajectory.title: Champions Trophy winner
trajectory.description: Part of India's ICC Men's Champions Trophy 2025 winning side in Dubai.

name: Shaheen Shah Afridi
milestone_by_age_26: Made T20I debut for Pakistan in April 2018 at age 18, becoming the first cricketer born after 2000 to represent Pakistan; completed all-format debuts in 2018, and was named ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year in 2021 at age 21, the first Pakistani to win the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy.
starting_point: Born April 6, 2000 in Landi Kotal, Khyber Agency, FATA (present-day Khyber District) into a Pashtun Zakhakhel Afridi tribe family; youngest of seven brothers. Eldest brother Riaz Afridi played a Test for Pakistan in 2004 and introduced Shaheen to hard-ball cricket at FATA U-16 trials in 2015.
current_position: Captain of Pakistan's ODI team; leads Lahore Qalandars in the PSL; first captain to win three PSL championships (2022, 2023, 2025); married to Ansha Afridi (Shahid Afridi's daughter) with son Aliyaar born 2024.

trajectory.title: U-16 tour of Australia
trajectory.description: Selected for Pakistan's Under-16 tour of Australia in November 2015 after being introduced to hard-ball cricket by his brother Riaz at FATA U-16 trials.

trajectory.title: Spectacular first-class debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-class debut for Khan Research Laboratories in the 2017-18 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, taking 8 wickets for 39 runs in the second innings, the best figures by a Pakistani bowler on first-class debut.

trajectory.title: T20I debut and all-format debuts
trajectory.description: Made his T20I debut against West Indies in April 2018, becoming the first cricketer born after 2000 to represent Pakistan; completed ODI and Test debuts later in 2018.

trajectory.title: ICC World Cup breakthrough
trajectory.description: Took 16 wickets at the 2019 ICC World Cup including 6/35 against Bangladesh, becoming the youngest bowler to claim a five-wicket haul in a men's World Cup match.

trajectory.title: ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year, becoming the first Pakistani to win the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, highlighted by 78 wickets in 36 international games and a match-winning spell against India at the T20 World Cup.

trajectory.title: PSL championship as captain
trajectory.description: Led Lahore Qalandars to their first Pakistan Super League title in 2022 as captain.

trajectory.title: Back-to-back PSL titles
trajectory.description: Led Lahore Qalandars to a second consecutive PSL championship in 2023, becoming the first captain to win back-to-back titles.

trajectory.title: Third PSL title and ODI captaincy
trajectory.description: Won a third PSL championship with Lahore Qalandars in 2025; appointed ODI captain of Pakistan by the PCB in October 2025.

name: Syed Sumail Hassan
milestone_by_age_26: Won The International 2015 with Evil Geniuses at age 16, becoming the youngest player to win The International and the youngest esports player to surpass $1 million in career winnings.
starting_point: Born February 13, 1999 in Karachi, Pakistan; started playing Dota at age 8 at internet cafes. Family moved to Rosemont, Illinois in 2012 where he joined the North American Elite League and became the highest-rated player.
current_position: Professional Dota 2 player for Nigma Galaxy; active in competitive Dota 2 as of 2026.

trajectory.title: Moved to the United States
trajectory.description: Family moved from Pakistan to Rosemont, Illinois; began playing in the North American Elite League and quickly became the highest-rated player.

trajectory.title: Signed with Evil Geniuses
trajectory.description: Recruited by Evil Geniuses in January 2015 at age 15 after UNiVeRsE pushed for his signing, joining one of the most recognized esports organizations.

trajectory.title: Won The International 2015
trajectory.description: Won The International 2015 with Evil Geniuses at age 16, becoming the youngest player to win TI and the youngest esports player to surpass $1 million in career winnings with over $1.3 million in prize money.

trajectory.title: TI6 third place with EG
trajectory.description: Placed third at The International 2016 with Evil Geniuses, earning approximately $436,000 in prize money.

trajectory.title: TI8 third place
trajectory.description: Placed third at The International 2018 with Evil Geniuses, earning approximately $536,000.

trajectory.title: Left Evil Geniuses
trajectory.description: Departed EG after five years, briefly playing with his brother YawaR on Quincy Crew before joining OG in 2020.

trajectory.title: Joined Nigma Galaxy
trajectory.description: Signed with Nigma Galaxy in May 2022, beginning a multi-year stint with the organization.

trajectory.title: TI2025 with Nigma Galaxy
trajectory.description: Helped Nigma Galaxy reach 5th-6th place at The International 2025, the highest TI placement for any of his teams since 2015.

name: Topias Taavitsainen
milestone_by_age_26: Won The International 2018 with OG at age 20, coming from open qualifiers to claim the championship and over $11 million in prize money, then repeated as champion in 2019.
starting_point: Born April 14, 1998 in Haukipudas, Finland; began playing Dota 2 and climbed the European MMR leaderboard through streaming before being recruited to OG in 2018.
current_position: Retired from professional Dota 2 in September 2024 after playing for Tundra Esports; completed Finnish military service in 2025.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with SFT e-sports
trajectory.description: Began his professional Dota 2 career with brief stints at SFT e-sports and 5 Anchors, playing in lower-tier tournaments.

trajectory.title: Joined OG and won The International 2018
trajectory.description: Recruited by OG in June 2018 as an unproven newbie; won The International 2018 coming through open qualifiers, defeating PSG.LGD in the grand final and earning over $11 million.

trajectory.title: Back-to-back TI champion
trajectory.description: Won The International 2019 with OG on August 25, 2019, becoming the first two-time TI winner alongside teammates N0tail, Ceb, ana, and JerAx.

trajectory.title: Stepped back from competitive Dota
trajectory.description: Placed 7th-8th at The International 2021 and took a break from competitive Dota to focus on family after the birth of his first daughter.

trajectory.title: Joined Tundra Esports
trajectory.description: Returned to competitive Dota 2, joining Tundra Esports as a stand-in for The International 2023, replacing Sakka who went inactive due to health reasons.

trajectory.title: Retired from professional Dota 2
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive Dota 2 in September 2024 after The International 13 with Tundra Esports, ending an eight-year career with nearly $6 million in prize money.

name: The Kid Laroi
milestone_by_age_26: At age 18, his single 'Stay' with Justin Bieber topped the Billboard Hot 100 (August 2021), and his debut mixtape 'F*ck Love' reached #1 on the Billboard 200 (July 2021).
starting_point: Born August 17, 2003 in Waterloo, New South Wales, Australia; parents split when he was young, mother sold drugs to get by, uncle murdered in 2015. Grew up in project housing in Redfern, Sydney, couch-surfing with his mother.
current_position: Australian rapper and singer; released debut studio album 'The First Time' in 2023-2024 and embarked on a global headlining tour; based in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Started recording music
trajectory.description: Began recording raps over beats on his mother's phone and uploading them to SoundCloud, forming the duo 'Dream$Team' with Adelaide rapper DJ Marcus Jr.

trajectory.title: Development deal with Sony Music Australia
trajectory.description: Signed a development deal with Sony Music Australia at age 14 and co-hosted the Fernside Festival.

trajectory.title: Released debut EP '14 with a Dream'
trajectory.description: Released his debut EP '14 with a Dream' the day before his 15th birthday, featuring collaborations with Manu Crooks, B Wise, and Miracle; finished top five in Triple J Unearthed High.

trajectory.title: Signed with Grade A Productions/Columbia
trajectory.description: Signed with Lil Bibby's Grade A Productions in a joint venture with Columbia Records; toured with Juice WRLD across Australia.

trajectory.title: Released mixtape 'F*ck Love'
trajectory.description: Released debut mixtape 'F*ck Love' which reached #1 in Australia and the top ten in the US.

trajectory.title: 'Stay' topped Billboard Hot 100
trajectory.description: Single 'Stay' with Justin Bieber topped the Billboard Hot 100 in August 2021; 'F*ck Love' reached #1 on the Billboard 200 in July 2021; made Saturday Night Live debut.

trajectory.title: Released debut studio album 'The First Time'
trajectory.description: Released his debut studio album 'The First Time' and embarked on a massive global headlining tour, solidifying his transition from viral star to established artist.

name: James Maynard
milestone_by_age_26: At age 26, independently discovered the Maynard-Tao sieve method and proved bounded gaps between primes, solving one of the oldest problems in number theory.
starting_point: Born June 10, 1987 in the UK; undergraduate at Queens' College, Cambridge; completed DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford under Roger Heath-Brown.
current_position: Professor of Number Theory at the University of Oxford; Fields Medalist (2022); Fellow of the Royal Society.

trajectory.title: Completed DPhil at Oxford
trajectory.description: Completed his DPhil in mathematics at Balliol College, Oxford under the supervision of Roger Heath-Brown.

trajectory.title: Proved bounded gaps between primes
trajectory.description: Independently discovered the Maynard-Tao sieve method and proved bounded gaps between primes, solving one of the oldest problems in number theory.

trajectory.title: CRM-ISM Postdoctoral Fellow
trajectory.description: Began postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Montreal and Fellowship by Examination at Magdalen College, Oxford.

trajectory.title: Clay Research Fellowship
trajectory.description: Awarded a Clay Research Fellowship from the Clay Mathematics Institute (2015-2018).

trajectory.title: Professor at Oxford
trajectory.description: Appointed Professor of Number Theory (Title IV Professorship) at the University of Oxford.

trajectory.title: Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians for his contributions to analytic number theory, particularly the distribution of prime numbers and Diophantine approximation.

name: Akshay Venkatesh
milestone_by_age_26: At age 22, was named a Clay Research Fellow after completing his PhD at Princeton at 21; by 26, had received the Salem Prize and Packard Fellowship for his work on subconvexity of automorphic L-functions.
starting_point: Born 1981 in New Delhi, India; grew up in Perth, Australia; regarded as a child prodigy. Studied mathematics and physics at the University of Western Australia.
current_position: Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton; Fields Medalist (2018); Fellow of the Royal Society.

trajectory.title: Graduated from University of Western Australia
trajectory.description: Completed BSc in Mathematics and Physics at the University of Western Australia, winning the J.A. Woods Prize for best graduating student.

trajectory.title: PhD from Princeton
trajectory.description: Completed his PhD in Mathematics at Princeton University under the supervision of Peter Sarnak.

trajectory.title: Clay Research Fellowship
trajectory.description: Awarded a Clay Mathematics Institute Research Fellowship (2004-2006) and began as C.L.E. Moore Instructor at MIT.

trajectory.title: Salem Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Salem Prize for his contributions to analytic number theory.

trajectory.title: SASTRA Ramanujan Prize
trajectory.description: Awarded the SASTRA Ramanujan Prize for outstanding contributions to number theory.

trajectory.title: Faculty at Stanford
trajectory.description: Joined Stanford University as Associate Professor, later becoming full Professor.

trajectory.title: Infosys Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Infosys Prize in Mathematical Sciences.

trajectory.title: Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Rio de Janeiro for his synthesis of analytic number theory, homogeneous dynamics, topology, and representation theory.

trajectory.title: Professor at IAS
trajectory.description: Appointed Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton.

name: Manjul Bhargava
milestone_by_age_26: At age 22, won the AMS-MAA-SIAM Morgan Prize for outstanding undergraduate research, having published four substantial papers as a Harvard undergraduate.
starting_point: Born August 8, 1974 in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada to an Indian family; grew up on Long Island, New York. Mother Mira Bhargava is a mathematician at Hofstra University and was his first mathematics teacher. Completed all high school math by age 14.
current_position: Robert Gunning-Brandon Fradd Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University; Stieltjes Professor at Leiden University; Fields Medalist (2014); Fellow of the Royal Society.

trajectory.title: High school valedictorian
trajectory.description: Graduated as valedictorian from Plainedge High School and won the New York State Science Talent Search.

trajectory.title: Harvard AB and Morgan Prize
trajectory.description: Graduated summa cum laude from Harvard University in mathematics; won the AMS-MAA-SIAM Morgan Prize for outstanding undergraduate research, having published four substantial papers.

trajectory.title: PhD from Princeton
trajectory.description: Completed his PhD in Mathematics at Princeton University with thesis on higher composition laws.

trajectory.title: Joined Princeton faculty
trajectory.description: Appointed Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University after being a Clay Mathematics Institute Long-Term Prize Fellow.

trajectory.title: Clay Research Award and SASTRA Ramanujan Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Clay Research Award and the SASTRA Ramanujan Prize for his contributions to number theory.

trajectory.title: Cole Prize
trajectory.description: Awarded the AMS Cole Prize in Number Theory.

trajectory.title: Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Seoul for developing powerful new methods in the geometry of numbers, applied to count rings of small rank and bound the average rank of elliptic curves.

trajectory.title: Padma Bhushan
trajectory.description: Awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award.

name: Artur Avila
milestone_by_age_26: At age 21, completed his PhD at IMPA on bifurcations of unimodal transformations, having won IMO gold at 16 and completed his MS at 18; by 26, gave the Cours Peccot at the College de France.
starting_point: Born June 29, 1979 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; won IMO gold medal at 16 representing Brazil with essentially no team training. Offered a scholarship to study at IMPA (Instituto de Matematica Pura e Aplicada).
current_position: Professor at the University of Zurich, Switzerland; Fields Medalist (2014); also holds position at IMPA, Rio de Janeiro.

trajectory.title: IMO Gold Medal
trajectory.description: Won a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad in Toronto, Canada, representing Brazil with essentially no team training investment.

trajectory.title: Completed MS at IMPA
trajectory.description: Completed his Master's degree at the Instituto de Matematica Pura e Aplicada in Rio de Janeiro under Welington de Melo.

trajectory.title: PhD from IMPA
trajectory.description: Completed his PhD at IMPA with thesis on bifurcations of unimodal maps, co-authored a 100-page paper with de Melo and Lyubich proving a long-sought result.

trajectory.title: CNRS Chargé de recherche
trajectory.description: Qualified for the CNRS competition in France after two attempts, becoming a Chargé de recherche attached to the Laboratoire de Probabilités in Paris.

trajectory.title: Cours Peccot at Collège de France
trajectory.description: Gave the Cours Peccot at the Collège de France, recognizing outstanding young mathematicians.

trajectory.title: Salem Prize and CNRS Bronze Medal
trajectory.description: Received the Salem Prize and the Bronze Medal of the CNRS for his contributions to dynamical systems.

trajectory.title: Youngest CNRS Research Director
trajectory.description: Became the youngest Directeur de recherche at CNRS, France's highest research position.

trajectory.title: Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Seoul for his outstanding contributions to dynamical systems, analysis, and other areas.

trajectory.title: Professor at University of Zurich
trajectory.description: Appointed Professor at the University of Zurich while maintaining his position at IMPA.

name: Cao Yuan
